<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par51" />{{GHGmargin-letter|51|l}}
Elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} after prepositions is required by the Masora in {{GHGheb|text=בִּכָּֽשְׁלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=17}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִכָּ׳}}), {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽהָרֵג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=15}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽעָטֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11}}; also in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵֽעָנוֹת}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵֽרָאוֹת}}); in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=30}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵאוֹר}}). It is, however, extremely doubtful whether the ''infin. Qal'' of the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} is not rather intended in all these examples; it certainly is so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|m}}
2. Instead of the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the ultima of the imperfect, {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} often occurs in pause, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּגָּמַֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=15}} (with final {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=23|hidebook=1}} (with {{GHGheb|text=ק}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=5}} (with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}); see {{GHGpar|29|q}}. In the 2nd and 3rd plur. fem. {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} predominates, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּזָּכַ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=17}}; {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} occurs only in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָגֵ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=13}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עגן}}, and hence, with loss of the doubling, for {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָגֵ֫נָּה}}; cf. even {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽאָמַֽנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=4}}.—With ''Nûn paragogicum'' (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) in the 2nd and 3rd plur. masc. are found, {{GHGheb|text=יִלָּֽכְדוּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּלָּֽחֲמוּן}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִבָּֽהֵלוּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּשָּֽׁמֵדוּן}}, &c.; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=24}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֵחָֽצְבֽוּן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|n}}
3. When the imperfect, the infinitive (in ''ē''), or the imperative is followed in close connexion by a monosyllable, or by a word with the gone on the first syllable, the tone is, as a rule (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאָֽבֵק אִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=25}}), shifted back from the ultima to the penultima, while the ultima, which thus loses the tone, takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִכָּ֫שֶׁל בָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּעָ֫תֶר לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=21}}; in the imperative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}.—So always {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫מֶר לְךָ}} (since {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ}} counts as ''one'' syllable) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=6}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=2}}; and even with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the ultima, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּעָ֫זַב אָ֑רֶץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=4}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּעָֽתֵ֫ר אֱלֹהִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=14}}). Although in isolated cases (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=23}}) the tone is not thrown back, in spite of a tone-syllable following, the retraction has become usual in certain forms, even when the next word begins with a toneless syllable; especially after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} {{GHGterm|consec.}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשָּׁ֫אֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלָּ֫חֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=1}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּצָּ֫מֶד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; and always so in the imperative {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=21}}, and (before Metheg of the counter-tone) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=9}}. On the avoidance of pausal-forms in the imperative ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=12}} with ''Silluq'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=11}} with ''Athnaḥ''), and imperfect ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=4}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|29|o}}, and note; on the other hand, always {{GHGheb|text=הִמָּלֵט}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּלֵט}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|o}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִקְבְּצוּ}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּֽבְצוּ}}, with the rejection of the initial {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=9}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Joel|chapter=4|verse=11}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נִקְבָּ֑צוּ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נִלְווּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=5}}); but in these examples either the reading or the explanation is doubtful. The 2nd sing. imperat. of {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁבַּע}} is always (with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogicum}}) {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫בְעָה לִּי|translate=swear to me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23}}, &c. (also {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁבְעָה לִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=15}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|p}}
4. For the 1st sing. of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=אִקָּטֵל}} is as frequent as {{GHGheb|text=אֶקָּטֵל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִדָּרֵשׁ|translate=I shall be inquired of}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁבֵעַ|translate=I will swear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=36}}, and so always in the cohortative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִנָּֽקְמָה|translate=I will avenge me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}, and in the impf. Niph. of {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} ({{GHGpar|69|t}}). The Babylonian punctuation admits only ''ĭ'' under the preformative of the 1st person.
<section end="par51" />
<section begin="par52" />{{GHGpar-heading|52|Piʿēl and Puʿal}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|a}}
'''1.''' The ''characteristic'' of this conjugation consists in the strengthening of the middle radical. From the simple stem ''qaṭal'' (cf. {{GHGpar|43|b}}) the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטַּל}} (cf. the Arabic conj. ii. ''qăttălă'') would naturally follow as<section end="par52" /><noinclude>
